podcast.title: Death from Systemic Lupus (2022)
podcast.body: In March 2018, Julee Cruise announced on Facebook that she was suffering from systemic lupus, experiencing severe pain and mobility issues, which led to a deep depression. She ultimately chose to end her life in a "controlled way" on June 9, 2022. Her husband reported that she passed away "on her own terms, no regrets, she is at peace," with The B-52s song "Rome" playing as she drifted off. "In March 2018, she announced on Facebook that she had systemic lupus and was living in a lot of pain. She found it hard to walk and stand, which sent her into a deep depression. And then she took her own life in a controlled way on June 9, 2022."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Association with David Lynch and Twin Peaks
podcast.body: Julee Cruise gained prominence in the 1990s through her extensive musical contributions to director David Lynch's Twin Peaks projects, with her music featured throughout the TV series. "Julie had a nice run in the 1990s thanks to her association with director David Lynch and specifically his Twin Peaks projects. Her music was all over those TV series."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Broadway Career
podcast.body: Beyond her music, Julee Cruise also performed on Broadway as both an actor and singer, including a notable role portraying Janis Joplin. "Julie also appeared on Broadway as an actor and singer, including a role where she played Janice Chaplin."

podcast.title: Collaboration with David Lynch
podcast.body: Julee Cruise's singular major hit, "Falling," was a result of her collaboration with filmmaker David Lynch. Lynch commissioned the instrumental version for his TV series "Twin Peaks" and subsequently had Cruise record the vocal rendition. "He needed something appropriately surreal for the 1989 TV show Twin Peaks. He commissioned songwriter Angela Battlemente, who created an instrumental falling."

podcast.title: Poor Health and Depression from Systemic Lupus
podcast.body: By 2018, Julee Cruise was in poor health due to systemic lupus, an autoimmune disease that caused significant pain and eventually left her unable to walk or stand, leading to a deep depression. "By 2018 she was in poor health as a result of systemic lupus, an autoimmune disease that caused her much pain. Soon she became unable to walk or stand, sending her into a deep depression."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

podcast.title: Post-Hit Career and Performances
podcast.body: Despite "Falling" being her only true hit, Julee Cruise released several more albums and ventured into acting. She also toured extensively with The B-52s between 1992 and 1999, stepping in when regular member Cindy Wilson was unavailable, and made guest appearances on other artists' albums. "Alas, it was the only thing for Julie despite releasing several more albums. But that was okay because she got several acting gigs and toured with the B-52s when regular member Cindy Wilson was unavailable between 1992 and 1999."

podcast.title: Suicide and Final Moments
podcast.body: Julee Cruise died by suicide on June 9th at the age of 65, with her husband playing "Rome," her favorite B-52's song, during her final moments. "Her end came on June 9th at the age of 65. She took her own life with her husband playing Rome, her favorite B-52 song."

xref.title: Death (January 2025) – Cardiac Arrest at 78, Aggravated by Emphysema and California Wildfires
xref.body: Filmmaker and musician David Lynch died at age 78 of cardiac arrest, a condition aggravated by emphysema and the California wildfires. As a musician, he produced the influential album *Floating Into the Night* by Julee Cruise. "Died at 78 of a cardiac arrest aggravated by emphysema and the California wildfires."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: "Twin Peaks" Soundtrack Collaboration
xref.body: Lynch's collaboration with composer Angelo Badalamenti and singer Julee Cruise, which began with "Blue Velvet," extended to the TV series "Twin Peaks." He had a specific dreamy and spooky atmosphere in mind for the show, which they helped bring to life through its soundtrack.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Failed Song Licensing for "Blue Velvet"
xref.body: For his 1986 film "Blue Velvet," Lynch attempted to license "Song to the Siren" by This Mortal Coil from 4AD, but the label refused. This led him to collaborate with Angelo Badalamenti and Julee Cruise for the film's soundtrack.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Floating Into the Night – Julee Cruise Production
xref.body: Lynch produced this album for singer Julee Cruise, which is described as influential. "He produced the influential album 'Floating Into the Night' by Julee Cruise."
